'''Joseph Bernstein''' (sometimes spelled '''I. N. Bernshtein'''; {{langx|he|יוס(י)ף נאומוביץ ברנשטיין}}; {{langx|ru|Иосиф Наумович Бернштейн}}; born 18 April 1945) is a Soviet-born Israeli [[mathematician]] working at [[Tel Aviv University]]. He works in [[algebraic geometry]], [[representation theory]], and [[number theory]].

== Biography ==
Bernstein received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in 1972 under [[Israel Gelfand]] at [[Moscow State University]]. In 1981, he emigrated to the United States due to growing [[antisemitism]] in the Soviet Union.<ref>[http://www.thecrimson.com/article/1983/2/25/a-refugee-at-harvard-psoviet-mathematician/ ''A Refugee at Harvard — Harvard's Scientific Minds: Soviet Researcher Joins the Math Department''], The Harvard Crimson, February 25, 1983.</ref> 
Bernstein was a professor at [[Harvard University|Harvard]] during 1983-1993. 
He was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in 1985-86 and again in 1997-98.<ref>[http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/ Institute for Advanced Study: A Community of Scholars]</ref> In 1993, he moved to Israel to take a professorship at Tel Aviv University (emeritus since 2014).

==Awards and honors==
Bernstein received a [[gold medal]] at the 1962 [[International Mathematical Olympiad]].<ref>{{IMO results|id=9831}}</ref> He was elected to the [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities]] in 2002 and was elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] in 2004. In 2004, Bernstein was awarded the [[Israel Prize]] for mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web| title = Israel Prize Official Site (in Hebrew) – Recipient's C.V. | url = http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/Tashsad/YosefBernstein/KorotHaimYosefBernstain.htm}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| title = Israel Prize Official Site (in Hebrew) – Judges' Rationale for Grant to Recipient | url = http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/Tashsad/YosefBernstein/NimokyHsoftim.htm}}</ref> In 1998, he was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Bernstein, Joseph|chapter=Analytic structures on representation spaces of reductive groups|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. II|year=1998|pages=519–525|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011689000}}</ref> In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref>
